Check the current health of checked catalog layers

Source: R/catalog-health.R
tbod_check_catalog.Rd

Checks current public ArcGIS endpoints and saved schemas for selected entries in the bundled checked catalog. It contacts publisher services and returns a report without changing the catalog or saving files. A healthy result is a point-in-time metadata check, not a measure of record freshness.

Usage

tbod_check_catalog(
  jurisdiction = "all",
  ids = NULL,
  timeout = 10,
  total_timeout = 1800,
  pause = 0.25,
  probe_query = FALSE
)

Arguments

jurisdiction

One checked-catalog jurisdiction code or "all".

ids

Optional nonempty vector of unique checked dataset IDs within jurisdiction; NULL checks all selected entries.

timeout

Per-HTTP-attempt timeout in seconds.

total_timeout

Maximum elapsed seconds for the complete check, including requests, retries, and pauses. Defaults to 1,800; Inf disables the overall deadline. Entries not reached are reported as unknown.

pause

Delay from 0 to 30 seconds between entries to limit request rate; defaults to 0.25. With probe_query = TRUE, also pauses between layer metadata and the count probe.

probe_query

Run a zero-match count query after usable metadata to verify Query capability. Defaults to FALSE for the existing metadata-only behavior. Query probes do not retrieve features.

Value

A tibble with one row per selected entry and publisher, jurisdiction, dataset_id, endpoint, checked_at (UTC POSIXct), status (healthy, unavailable, schema_changed, unsupported, or unknown), failure_type, http_status, service_status and layer_status (available, unavailable, or unknown), schema_status (unchanged, compatible, incompatible, or unavailable), schema_issues (a list of issue tibbles), and details. health_state summarizes status as healthy, degraded, unavailable, or unknown. response_time_ms is elapsed request time including retries and a missing-layer service-root probe, excluding deliberate pauses; it is missing if no request was made. query_status is not_checked, verified, failed, or unknown; query_failure_type, query_http_status, and query_details explain a failed or uncertain probe. http_status is missing when no metadata HTTP response was received.

Details

Each entry starts one layer-metadata request. The client probes the service root only after a missing-layer response (HTTP or ArcGIS 404/410, or an explicit layer-not-found error) to distinguish a missing layer from a missing service. Transient failures remain unknown after bounded retries; entries not reached before total_timeout are also unknown. The default retry limit is three additional attempts per retryable failure sequence. Set options(tampaBayOpenData.max_retries = 3L) to change it (whole number from 0 to 10).

healthy means the layer metadata is valid, Query is advertised, and the schema matches the saved snapshot. schema_changed includes both compatible and incompatible drift; inspect schema_status and schema_issues. Confirmed schema drift remains schema_changed if Query capability is unreported. With no saved baseline, schema_status is unavailable and status is unknown. A missing object-ID field is reported as schema drift when a baseline exists; the details also identify unsupported record retrieval. unsupported includes layers that cannot be queried and access failures. By default the check does not retrieve features or run count and object-ID queries. A layer can advertise Query yet fail those operations during retrieval. Set probe_query = TRUE to run a zero-match count request after valid layer metadata; it reads no features and records whether the actual Query operation succeeds. A confirmed query failure is degraded, while a transient probe failure is unknown unless independently confirmed schema drift already makes the result degraded. The result cannot guarantee future service availability.

Examples

if (identical(Sys.getenv("TAMPA_OPEN_DATA_LIVE"), "true")) {
  report <- tbod_check_catalog(ids = "construction-permits")
  report[, c("dataset_id", "status", "schema_status", "details")]
}
